facts.statement: The genus Garudimimus was formally described by Rinchen Barsbold in 1981.
facts.quote: authority: Barsbold, 1981

facts.statement: Garudimimus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Garudimimus was found in 1981 by a Soviet-Mongolian expedition in the Bayanshiree Formation.
facts.quote: The genus is known from a single specimen found in 1981 by a Soviet-Mongolian paleontological expedition in the Bayanshiree Formation

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton was discovered in 1981 at Bayshin Tsav in the Bayan Shireh Formation of Southeastern Mongolia.
facts.quote: In 1981, during a Soviet-Mongolian paleontological expedition to the Gobi Desert, a relatively small theropod skeleton was discovered by the team at Bayshin Tsav in the Late Cretaceous Bayan Shireh Formation, Southeastern Mongolia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is catalogued as MPC-D 100/13.
facts.quote: The remains are catalogued as MPC-D 100/13

facts.statement: The generic name Garudimimus refers to the legendary Garuda and the Latin word for mimic.
facts.quote: The generic name, Garudimimus, combines a reference to Garuda which are legendary winged creatures from Mongolian Buddhist mythology and Latin mimus (meaning mimic).

facts.statement: The specific name brevipes refers to the short metatarsus of the animal.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from Latin brevis (meaning short) and pes (meaning foot), referring to the short metatarsus.

facts.statement: The only known species of Garudimimus is Garudimimus brevipes.
facts.quote: The only species is Garudimimus brevipes.

facts.statement: Garudimimus is grouped within the family Deinocheiridae as the sister taxon to Deinocheirus.
facts.quote: it was found that the latter was the sister taxon of Garudimimus, grouping within the Deinocheiridae

facts.statement: The placement of Garudimimus within the Deinocheiridae is disputed.
facts.quote: This placement has been disputed, though.

facts.statement: The known specimen of Garudimimus measured nearly 3.5 meters in length and weighed between 77.3 and 98 kilograms.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of Garudimimus was a medium-sized animal measuring nearly 3.5 m in length and weighing about 77.3 - 98 kg.

facts.statement: Garudimimus was an ornithomimosaur possessing a mix of basal and derived anatomical features.
facts.quote: It was an ornithomimosaur with a mix of basal and derived features

facts.statement: Garudimimus had toothless upper and lower jaws, unlike primitive ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: unlike primitive ornithomimosaurs, both upper and lower jaws were toothless

facts.statement: Garudimimus had relatively short, stocky hindlimbs, robust feet, and reduced ilia.
facts.quote: Garudimimus had relatively short and stocky hindlimbs, robust feet, and a reduced ilia.

facts.statement: Garudimimus had four toes on its foot with the first toe very reduced, unlike the three-toed ornithomimids.
facts.quote: The foot had four toes with the first one very reduced, whereas ornithomimids were three-toed with the first toe lost.

facts.statement: Garudimimus had a toothless skull with straight jaws ending in a rounded snout tip.
facts.quote: The toothless skull has very straight jaws ending in a more rounded snout tip than that of other genera.

facts.statement: It was previously thought that Garudimimus had a lacrimal horn, but redescription showed this was a distorted prefrontal bone.
facts.quote: It was previously thought that this primitive ornithomimosaurian possessed a lacrimal "horn" at the top of the skull, in front of the eye socket. However, the redescription of the only specimen has shown that this structure was simply the distorted left prefrontal bone.

facts.statement: Early interpretations suggested Garudimimus had an arctometatarsalian condition in its metatarsus.
facts.quote: Another early interpretation was the metatarsus reconstructed with an arctometatarsalian condition.

facts.statement: Some researchers claimed Garudimimus possessed a nasal horn similar to that of Pelecanimimus.
facts.quote: In 1994, Bernardino P. Pérez-Moreno with colleagues described the primitive ornithomimosaur Pelecanimimus and identified the presence of a crest in the holotype specimen. They claimed a similar trait in Garudimimus which was represented by a nasal horn.

facts.statement: A 2005 redescription by Kobayashi and Barsbold refuted many previous interpretations of Garudimimus anatomy.
facts.quote: In a comprehensive redescription in 2005 at the hands of Yoshitsugu Kobayashi and Barsbold, numerous of the previous statements were refuted.

facts.statement: Kobayashi showed that Garudimimus lacked an arctometatarsalian condition and had different metatarsal ratios than Archaeornithomimus.
facts.quote: Moreover, Kobayashi previously showed that in addition to actually lacking an arctometatarsalian condition, the metatarsal ratios are different to Archaeornithomimus.

facts.statement: Garudimimus was an omnivore or herbivore with a reduced bite force compensated by a horny beak.
facts.quote: Like other members of Ornithomimosauria, Garudimimus was an omnivore/herbivore with a reduced bite force that was compensated by a horny beak.

facts.statement: The pelvic girdle and hindlimbs of Garudimimus indicate poor cursorial (running) capacities.
facts.quote: therefore, indicating poor cursorial capacities.

facts.statement: Unfused vertebrae suggest the holotype specimen was a still-growing sub-adult animal.
facts.quote: Several unfused vertebrae indicates that the holotype was likely a still-growing sub-adult animal.

facts.statement: Garudimimus likely had shaggy feathering similar to large paleognath birds like ratites.
facts.quote: Based on feather impressions of several specimens of Ornithomimus, Garudimimus likely developed a shaggy feathering mostly similar to that of large paleognath birds such as ratites.

facts.statement: Garudimimus lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Garudimimus (meaning "Garuda mimic") is a genus of ornithomimosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Garudimimus possessed a small skull relative to its body size and lacked teeth in both jaws.
facts.quote: Garudimimus had a rather small skull in proportion to the overall skeleton, and both jaws were edentulous (devoid of teeth).

facts.statement: The skull of Garudimimus measured approximately 25 cm in length and 4.6 cm in width.
facts.quote: The skull was about 25 cm long with a width of 4.6 cm.

facts.statement: The toothless jaws and numerous surface holes suggest Garudimimus had a prominent horny beak during its life.
facts.quote: The edentulous condition of both premaxilla and dentary with the addition of numerous foramina in their surfaces, indicate that a prominent rhamphotheca (horny beak) was present in life.

facts.statement: The dentary bone, the longest part of the lower jaw, measured 18.3 cm and was thickened at its posterior end.
facts.quote: The dentary was the longest mandibular element measuring 18.3 cm long and was thickened towards the end.

facts.statement: The axis vertebra was short, measuring about 3 cm in length and 1.8 cm in height, likely representing a primitive trait for ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: The central length of the axis was rather short, measuring approximately 3 cm long and 1.8 cm high—probably a primitive condition in ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: The sacrum of Garudimimus consisted of six vertebrae, with the first and sixth having ribs attached to the inner ilium.
facts.quote: The sacrum was composed of six sacral vertebrae of which the first and sixth had sacral ribs attached to the inner surface of the ilium.

facts.statement: The total length of the sacrum was approximately 31 cm, nearly matching the length of the ilium.
facts.quote: The total length of the sacrum (31 cm) was nearly equal to that of the ilium.

facts.statement: Unlike other members of its group, the sacral vertebrae of Garudimimus were not air-spaced.
facts.quote: Unlike other ornithomimosaurs, the sacral vertebrae lacked pneumatization (air-spaced).

facts.statement: The pubis was a large bone measuring 39 cm in length, featuring a straight shaft and a prominent projection at the end.
facts.quote: The pubis was a large element measuring 39 cm in length. It had a nearly straight shaft and a prominent pubic boot (large projection at the end).

facts.statement: The femur was relatively straight, measured 37.1 cm in length, and had a well-developed head with a flattened shaft.
facts.quote: The femur was relatively straight and had a length of 37.1 cm. It had a well-developed femoral head and a sideways flattened shaft.

facts.statement: Garudimimus differed from typical ornithomimids by possessing five metatarsals in its foot.
facts.quote: In the pes (foot) formula, Garudimimus strongly differed from the ornithomimid condition by having five metatarsals.

facts.statement: The third metatarsal was the longest in the foot, measuring 22.9 cm.
facts.quote: The third metatarsal was the longest (22.9 cm long).

facts.statement: Garudimimus had four toes on its feet, with the first toe being the smallest.
facts.quote: The feet had four primitive digits (toes) with the first being the smallest.

facts.statement: The claw bones of the feet were recurved and had prominent tendon attachments, differing from the straight claws of other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Pedal unguals (claw bones) had a recurved shape that differed from the straight shape in ornithomimids, and prominent flexor tubercles (flexor tendons attachments).

facts.statement: The lower edges of the premaxilla bone were thin and sharply developed.
facts.quote: The bottom edges of the premaxilla were thin and sharply-developed.

facts.statement: The ilium was a large but short bone compared to ornithomimids, characterized by a hook-shaped front end.
facts.quote: The ilium was a large bone—yet short compared to ornithomimids—with a hook-shaped anterior end.

facts.statement: It is debated whether large holes and deep depressions on the front neural arches indicate that the tail bones were air-spaced.
facts.quote: Putative large foramen and deep fossae (depressions) were present on the anterior neural arches, which may indicate caudal pneumaticity in Garudimimus.

facts.statement: In 1981, Barsbold classified Garudimimus in its own family, Garudimimidae.
facts.quote: In 1981, Barsbold assigned Garudimimus to a separate Garudimimidae given the unusual traits in the taxon.

facts.statement: Kobayashi and Barsbold identified that Garudimimus shared traits like four-toed feet and toothless jaws with other ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: Kobayashi and Barsbold noted that this taxon shared traits with primitive and derived ornithomimosaurs such as four-toed feet and toothless jaws.

facts.statement: In 2019, Hartman and colleagues performed a phylogenetic analysis of Coelurosauria that included ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: In 2019 Hartman and colleagues described the new paravian Hesperornithoides performing an extensive phylogenetic analysis for the Coelurosauria.

facts.statement: In 2020, Serrano-Brañas and colleagues described the new deinocheirid genus Paraxenisaurus.
facts.quote: In 2020, Serrano-Brañas and team described and named the new deinocheirid genus Paraxenisaurus from the Cerro del Pueblo Formation.

facts.statement: An analysis of scleral rings indicated that Garudimimus was a cathemeral herbivore.
facts.quote: The results indicated that Garudimimus was a cathemeral herbivore with other predatory theropods being mainly nocturnal.

facts.statement: In 2005, Kobayashi and Barsbold noted that Garudimimus lacked teeth on its lower jaw and had a recurved jaw shape, making its feeding habits more similar to ornithomimids than other primitive ornithomimosaurs.
facts.quote: Kobayashi and Barsbold stated in 2005 that the absence of dentition on the lower jaw and the recurved shape of the same indicates that Garudimimus was fairly more similar to ornithomimids when consuming food than to other primitive ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: The front parts of Garudimimus's upper and lower jaws were covered by a beak that likely helped it pluck food.
facts.quote: Like ornithomimids, the anterior parts of the upper and lower jaws of Garudimimus were both covered by a beak and may have been used for plucking food.

facts.statement: Garudimimus is widely considered a herbivore or at least an omnivore based on its unique anatomical features, such as the presence of a beak.
facts.quote: Moreover, Garudimimus and kin are widely regarded as herbivore or at least omnivore dinosaurs by their peculiar anatomical traits—including the presence of a beak.

facts.statement: Researchers Cuff and Rayfield suggested that the low bite force measured in Garudimimus might be due to the use of a different species' jaw in reconstructions or because the specimen was a sub-adult.
facts.quote: Cuff and Rayfield pointed out that the bite force of Garudimimus may be limited for having to use the mandible of Struthiomimus in the reconstructions or that MPC-D 100/13 is a sub-adult individual.

facts.statement: Cuff and Rayfield tentatively concluded that Garudimimus used its low bite force and beak to hold plant material while its neck muscles plucked vegetation.
facts.quote: Tentatively, they agreed in that relatively low bite forces combined with a rhamphotheca could be used to hold plant material during feeding in ornithomimosaurs, all of this whilst neck musculature provided enough force to pluck away vegetation.

facts.statement: Button and Zanno noted that there is no consistent relationship between herbivory and body size in ornithomimosaurs, as larger size does not always correlate with herbivory in this group.
facts.quote: However, Button and Zanno pointed out that the relationship between herbivory and size is not always related and there is no lineal trend of increasing mass in ornithomimosaurs.

facts.statement: Button and Zanno concluded that similar feeding strategies evolved independently in unrelated herbivorous dinosaur lineages over time.
facts.quote: Button and Zanno concluded that feeding strategies convergently evolved in unrelated herbivorous dinosaurs over the time.

facts.statement: Nabavizadeh described ornithomimosaurs, including Garudimimus, as orthal feeders that raised their jaws isognathously so that upper and lower teeth on each side contacted simultaneously.
facts.quote: Nabavizadeh noted that ornithomimosaurs were orthal feeders and raised their jaws isognathously whereby the upper and lower teeth of each side occluded (contacted each other) at once.

facts.statement: Garudimimus and Deinocheirus possess unique jaw muscle attachment sites featuring a triangular adductor complex attached to an expanding surangular bone.
facts.quote: Deinocheirus and Garudimimus have unique attachment sites for the muscles that open and close the jaws, which are composed by a downwards-expanded, triangular adductor musculature complex attaching to a forwards expanding surangular bone.

facts.statement: Garudimimus fossils were found in the Late Cretaceous Bayan Shireh Formation at the Bayshin Tsav locality.
facts.quote: The known remains of Garudimimus were unearthed from the Late Cretaceous Bayan Shireh Formation at the Bayshin Tsav locality.

facts.statement: The Bayan Shireh Formation, where Garudimimus was found, dates from approximately 95.9 ± 6.0 to 89.6 ± 4.0 million years ago, spanning the Cenomanian to Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Using calcite U–Pb measurements, the age of the Bayan Shireh Formation has been dated from about 95.9 ± 6.0 million to 89.6 ± 4.0 million years ago during the Cenomanian-Santonian stages.

facts.statement: The Bayan Shireh Formation was deposited by meandering rivers and large water bodies on an alluvial plain under a semi-arid climate.
facts.quote: The presence of caliche, fluvial and lacustrine sedimentation at various localities indicates that this formation was deposited by meandering rivers and other large water bodies on an alluvial plain (flat land consisting of sediments deposited by highland rivers) under a semi-arid climate.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests that the water bodies in the Bayan Shireh Formation drained the eastern part of the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: Numerous scale-like cross-stratifications at the Baynshire locality are indicators of large meanders, and the vast majority of these water bodies may have drained the eastern part of the Gobi Desert.

facts.statement: Numerous authors have proposed a correlation between the Bayan Shireh Formation and the Iren Dabasu Formation based on similar fossil assemblages.
facts.quote: Based on the similar fossil assemblages, a correlation between the Bayan Shireh and Iren Dabasu formations has been proposed by numerous authors.

facts.statement: Garudimimus lived alongside herbivorous ornithischians including Gobihadros, Graciliceratops, and Talarurus.
facts.quote: Garudimimus shared its habitat with multiple dinosaurian fauna, such as the herbivorous ornithischians Gobihadros, Graciliceratops and Talarurus.

facts.statement: The ecosystem included theropods such as the tyrannosauroid Khankhuuluu, the dromaeosaurid Achillobator, and the therizinosaurids Erlikosaurus and Segnosaurus.
facts.quote: Other theropods are represented by the tyrannosauroid Khankhuuluu, the large dromaeosaurid Achillobator, and the therizinosaurids Erlikosaurus and Segnosaurus.

facts.statement: Therizinosaurs were among the most abundant theropods in the Bayan Shireh Formation, with many described and undescribed specimens.
facts.quote: In terms of biodiversity, therizinosaurs were some of the most abundant theropods with multiple described and undescribed specimens across the formation.

facts.statement: Although Garudimimus is the only named ornithomimosaur, the Bayan Shireh Formation contains locally abundant remains of this group.
facts.quote: Though Garudimimus is currently the only ornithomimosaur taxon named, the Bayan Shireh Formation has produced locally abundant ornithomimosaurs at Bayshin Tsav.

facts.statement: The genus Garudimimus was named by Barsbold in 1981.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Barsbold, 1981

facts.statement: The species Garudimimus brevipes was named by Barsbold in 1981.
facts.quote: species_authority: Barsbold, 1981

facts.statement: Garudimimus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 98 to 90 million years ago, between the Cenomanian and Turonian stages, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 98 y 90 millones de años, entre el Cenomaniense y el Turoniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Garudimimus fossils were found in Bayshin Tsav, Mongolia.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se encontraron en Bayshin Tsav (Mongolia).

facts.statement: Garudimimus was a relatively small ornithomimosaur.
facts.quote: Garudimimus era un ornitomimosauriano relativamente pequeño.

facts.statement: The length of the femur is 371 millimeters.
facts.quote: La longitud del fémur es de 371 milímetros.

facts.statement: It had relatively short legs, heavy feet, and the shortest ilium in the hip region.
facts.quote: Tenía piernas relativamente cortas, pies pesados y en la cadera, el ilion más corto

facts.statement: The foot had four toes and a vestige of the first digit.
facts.quote: El pie tenía cuatro dedos y un vestigio del primer dígito

facts.statement: The toothless skull had very straight jaws ending in a more rounded snout tip than other group members, and larger eyes.
facts.quote: El cráneo sin dientes tiene mandíbulas muy rectas que terminan en una punta de hocico más redondeada que la de otras personas del grupo, y ojos más grandes.

facts.statement: Recent studies showed that the supposed lacrimal horn was actually the sharp posterior end of a misplaced nasal bone.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estudios recientes han demostrado que este "cuerno" era simplemente el extremo posterior afilado y afilado del hueso nasal mal ubicado.

facts.statement: In 1981, a Soviet expedition in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia discovered a theropod skeleton at Baishin Tsav in Ömnögovi Province.
facts.quote: En 1981, durante una expedición soviética en Mongolia hasta el desierto de Gobi, un esqueleto terópodo fue descubierto en Baishin Tsav en provincia de Ömnögovi, Mongolia.

facts.statement: In the same year, Rinchen Barsbold named and described the type species Garudimimus brevipes.
facts.quote: El mismo año este espécimen fue nombrado y descrito por Rinchen Barsbold, como la especie tipo Garudimimus brevipes.

facts.statement: The genus name combines a reference to the Garuda, a winged creature from Mongolian Buddhist mythology, with the Latin term mimus, meaning "imitate".
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina una referencia a la Garuda, criatura alada de la mitología budista de Mongolia, con el término en latín mimus, "imitar".

facts.statement: The specific name derives from the Latin brevis, meaning "short," and pes, meaning "foot," referring to its short metatarsus.
facts.quote: El nombre específico se deriva del latín brevis, "cortos", y pes, "pie", en referencia a su corto metatarso.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, GIN 100/13, was found in Upper Cretaceous sediments of the Bayan Shireh Formation.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, GIN 100/13, fue descubierto en sedimentos del Cretácico superior de la formación Bayan Shireh

facts.statement: Its possible age range spans from the Cenomanian to the Campanian.
facts.quote: Su posible rango de edad va desde el Cenomaniano hasta el Campaniano.

facts.statement: It consists of a fairly complete and articulated skeleton including the skull but lacking the shoulder girdle, forelimbs, and tail tip, belonging to a subadult individual.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto bastante completo y articulado que incluye el cráneo pero que carece de la cintura escapular, las extremidades anteriores y el extremo de la cola, de un individuo subadulto.

facts.statement: The skeleton was first described in detail in works by Yoshitsugu Kobayashi in 2004 and 2005.
facts.quote: El esqueleto se describió por primera vez en detalle en obras de Yoshitsugu Kobayashi de 2004 y 2005.

facts.statement: In 1981, Rinchen Barsbold assigned Garudimimus to a separate family, Garudimimidae, due to unusual morphological features.
facts.quote: En 1981, a raíz de las inusuales características morfológicas que presentaban los restos fósiles, Rinchen Barsbold asignó a Garudimimus a una familia separada, Garudimimidae.

facts.statement: In 2014, Yuong-Nam Lee determined Garudimimus as a sister taxon to Deinocheirus, assigning it to the family Deinocheiridae and synonymizing Garudimimidae with Deinocheiridae.
facts.quote: En 2014 Garudimimus fue determinado como un taxón hermano a Deinocheirus por Yuong-Nam Lee y por lo tanto fue asignado a la familia Deinocheiridae sinonimizando Garudimimidae con Deinocheiridae.

facts.statement: The time range is the Turonian to Santonian stages, from 93.9 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Santonian (93.9 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: It was previously thought that this primitive member of Ornithomimosauria possessed a lacrimal horn on the top of the skull, in front of the eye socket.
facts.quote: Anteriormente se pensaba que este miembro "primitivo" de Ornithomimosauria poseía un cuerno lacrimal en la parte superior del cráneo, frente a la cuenca del ojo.

facts.statement: An initial error was Thomas Holtz's suggestion that the foot was incorrectly reconstructed and was actually arctometatarsalian.
facts.quote: Otro error inicial fue la sugerencia de Thomas Holtz de que el pie se había reconstruido incorrectamente y de hecho habría sido arctometatarsiano

facts.statement: Garudimimus was one of the earliest ornithomimosaurians and does not seem to have been as well adapted for speed as more derived ornithomimids.
facts.quote: Garudimimus fue uno de los primeros ornitomimosaurios y parece no haber sido tan adecuado para la velocidad como los ornitomímidos más derivados.

rejected.quote: Both tibia and fibula were nearly equal in length to the femur (36 cm and 38.8 cm respectively).

rejected.statement: In a 2014 analysis, Lee and colleagues grouped Beishanlong, Garudimimus, and Deinocheirus together in the family Deinocheiridae.
rejected.quote: Lee and team performed a large phylogenetic analysis for the Deinocheiridae and the three members were found in this grouping: Beishanlong, Garudimimus and Deinocheirus.

rejected.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the adult length at 2.5 meters and the weight at 30 kilograms.
